objective: Audit source-faithful permanent pins in V15's three-state menu CSP; classify the first path and cycle cores, preserve actual neighborhoods, and delimit exactly which local repair routes fail without claiming C1 or root closure.

atomic_claims.text: The V15 three-state menu CSP has exactly thirty ordered length-two empty-middle paths; every such core is repaired by recoloring its degree-two middle vertex, while exactly twenty-one leaf-unordered degree-three colored stars remain center-rigid.

Every one of the twenty-one center-rigid stars becomes menu-supported after recoloring one leaf when that leaf has no other fixed incidence; therefore a source-faithful permanent core must propagate to another terminal, a cycle, or a multiattachment region.

A terminal-free bridge branch cannot supply an absolute permanent pin in a vertex-minimal root obstruction: color its smaller side, translate the one attachment, and glue. Permanent-pin claims require a terminal-to-terminal, cyclic, or multiattachment certificate.

For rooted four-state identity-pin cycles, all twenty-seven C4 pins unpin by one nonroot recolor, whereas C5 has one hundred eighty pins and eighteen resist every one-vertex recolor and every uniform plus/minus-one shift of a nonroot subset; the representative 13-0-7-15-4 is repaired by a two-vertex move.
Domain deletion and bridge pruning have well-founded finite ranks, but one-vertex or unit-subset-shift availability is not a global potential, as witnessed by the frozen C5 core.

assumptions: The corrected V15 maps T8,T9,T10 and its exact edge-CSP semantics; the companion V16 identity-pin proof is candidate prior art on the same branch.
Every degree-three star and cycle is interpreted with actual vertex identities and all listed incident edges; a leaf is releasable only when no omitted fixed incidence constrains it.
Finite computations classify only the frozen menu-CSP objects and do not imply that every minimum counterexample contains one.
risks: No theorem shows that a genuine C1 minimum obstruction contains one of the classified rigid stars or C5 cores.
The representative C5 core has a two-vertex repair, so it is not an obstruction to all recolorings or a root counterexample.
The bridge-pruning statement requires a genuine one-attachment terminal-free component; cycles and multiattachments remain open.
All computation and proof drafting remain in the generator trust domain; no Lean, SMT, registered verifier, EvidenceLink, Result, or Solution admission occurred.
C1-C4 and both admitted obligations remain open.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: The rooted C5 coloring 13-0-7-15-4 is identity-pinned in the four-state menu CSP and resists every one-nonroot-vertex recolor and every uniform plus/minus-one shift of a nonroot subset. This rejects only that local unpinning family; a two-vertex repair exists.
